_readme: Interactive 3D model pages. tools/build_3d.py writes site/3d-<page>.html and site/sitemap-3d.xml from this file; build_learn.py (guides, Learn hub, search, llms.txt), build_catalogue.py (programme pages) and build_reels.py (Watch) read it for the 'See it in 3D' links. Follow docs/3D-SOP.md for every new model. 'guides' and 'programmes' must be pages that exist and mention the subject; 'sells' must be one of them. Tags: Measured, Documented, Comparative, Hypothetical, Reconstructed, Estimated, Illustrative.

models.label: Reconstruction from published surveys and plans. Estimated parts tagged.
models.title: Kandariya Mahadeva Temple in 3D | Talaash Heritage
models.description: Turn and zoom a 3D model of the Kandariya Mahadeva temple at Khajuraho, built from Cunningham's survey: 109 ft long and 116½ ft high, with every estimated part tagged.
models.og_description: The largest standing temple at Khajuraho, built from Cunningham's survey. Turn it, zoom in, see what is measured and what is estimated.
models.lede: The Kandariya Mahadeva is the largest standing temple at Khajuraho, built during the Chandela dynasty, who ruled the region in the 10th and 11th centuries CE. This model is built from the measurements Alexander Cunningham published from his 1864–65 survey and from his ground plan.
facts: About 18.1 m (59½ ft) externally; Fergusson gives 60 ft (18.3 m)
35.5 m (116½ ft) above the ground; 26.8 m (88 ft) above its own floor
8.7 m (28½ ft) above the ground: the difference between the two heights

Portico, hall (mandapa), great hall with transepts (maha-mandapa), vestibule (antarala) and sanctum (garbha-griha), with a passage round the sanctum lit by three open porticoes at the back and sides: a "double cross"
Each part has its own roof, rising in steps from the low pyramid over the entrance to the tall spire over the sanctum
A marble liṅga, shown here as a plain labelled shape
Cunningham counted 226 statues inside and 646 outside, 872 in all (not modelled)
Built during the Chandela dynasty, who ruled the region in the 10th and 11th centuries CE
Chamber sizes, wall and roof heights
Read from the published plan and photographs, not from a measured section
84 smaller replicas of the main spire (Krishna Deva). Their grouping in the model is estimated
How the 8.7 m rise divides between the shared terrace and the temple's own base
body: Cunningham describes the temple as having the usual portico, hall, great hall, vestibule and sanctum, "each of which has its separate pinnacled roof rising in regular gradation from the low pyramid of the entrance to the lofty spire of the sanctum". A second pair of transepts lights the passage round the sanctum, which is why he calls the plan a large double cross rather than a single one.

What the model does not show: the sculpture. Cunningham counted 872 statues on and in the temple, and no deity figures are modelled here. The sanctum holds a marble liṅga, drawn as a plain shape with a label.
models.visit: Khajuraho is in Madhya Pradesh. We teach the temples in a two-hour masterclass and walk them with you on site.
sources: A. Cunningham, Four Reports Made during the Years 1862-63-64-65, Archaeological Survey of India Reports vol. II (1871), pp. 419–420, and plate XCVII (plan).
Krishna Deva, Khajuraho (Archaeological Survey of India, World Heritage Series), full text.
D. N. Shukla, Vāstu-Śāstra (1960): the dimensions and the double-cross plan, quoted from an earlier survey.
J. Fergusson, History of Indian and Eastern Architecture, revised edition (1910), fig. 342: plan of the Kandariya Mahadeva after Cunningham, 50 ft to 1 in.
Archaeological Survey of India, World Heritage Sites: Khajuraho.
UNESCO World Heritage List no. 240, Khajuraho Group of Monuments.
Encyclopaedia Britannica, pradakshina (for the illustrative people walking round).

app.eyebrow: Khajuraho, Madhya Pradesh · Chandela, c. 1025–1050 CE (Krishna Deva)
app.heading: Kandariya Mahadeva Temple: an evidence-tagged 3D reconstruction
app.intro: Built at true scale from Alexander Cunningham's survey and plan. Every element and fact carries an evidence tag, and the sources are listed in the panel. Drag to orbit, right-drag or Shift-drag to pan, pinch to zoom (or click the model, then scroll). In walk mode, use WASD or the arrow keys, or the on-screen pad.

models.label: Reconstruction from published surveys. Estimated parts tagged.
models.title: Bhaja Caves Chaitya Hall (Cave 12) in 3D | Talaash Heritage
models.description: Walk round a 3D model of the rock-cut chaitya hall at Bhaja near Lonavala: 59 ft long, 27 pillars, a stupa and teak ribs, from the 1880 survey, with estimated parts tagged.
models.og_description: A rock-cut prayer hall near Lonavala, built from the 1880 survey: turn it, cut it open and see what is measured and what is estimated.
models.lede: Cave 12 at Bhaja, near Lonavala in Pune district, is an early rock-cut chaitya hall: a prayer hall with a stupa at the far end, cut into the west face of a hill. This model is built from the measurements in Fergusson and Burgess's The Cave Temples of India (1880) and the 1885 Bombay Gazetteer.
facts: Fergusson and Burgess (1880) put it at about 200 BCE or earlier; the 1885 Gazetteer puts the group in the 2nd and 1st centuries BCE
The caves are about 122 m (400 ft) above Bhaja village, in the west face of a steep hill
18.0 m (59 ft), with a semicircular apse at the back
8.13 m (26 ft 8 in) (Fergusson and Burgess); the 1885 Gazetteer gives about 29 ft (8.8 m)
8.05 m (26 ft 5 in) from the floor to the top of the vault
27 plain octagonal pillars, 3.45 m (11 ft 4 in) high, raking inward about 13 cm (5 in) on each side
Nave 4.98 m (16 ft 4 in) wide at the pillar bases and 4.72 m (15 ft 6 in) at their tops; aisles 1.04 m (3 ft 5 in)
Rises from a narrow ledge 2.26 m (7 ft 5 in) above the pillar tops; ribbed with teak, of which the first four ribs and parts of others had given way or been pulled down by 1880
3.35 m (11 ft) across at the floor; drum 1.22 m (4 ft) high; dome 1.83 m (6 ft) high; a two-storeyed box on top with a hole 18 cm (7 in) across and about 51 cm (20 in) deep
Entirely of wood: four holes in the floor for the main uprights, mortices in the arch for a cross-beam, about 170 pin holes in three rows on the great arch
The 1880 and 1885 surveys record carved symbols on four pillars but no image of the Buddha
The screen, doors and lattice as drawn here: only the sockets, mortices and pin holes survive
Pillar and rib spacing, box sizes, aisle ceiling, rock outside the hall
body: The hall was not all rock. Its vault was lined with teak ribs, and Fergusson and Burgess concluded that the front must have been entirely of wood: four holes in the floor, mortices in the arch and some 170 pin holes show where it was fixed. None of that woodwork survives, so the front in the model is marked hypothetical; switch it on with the Timber front button to see one possible form.
The stupa stands in the apse at the far end of the nave. The model shows no figures in the hall: the surveys record only a few carved symbols on four pillars.
models.visit: Bhaja is near Lonavala in Pune district, Maharashtra. We cover it in our guide to India's Buddhist caves and on heritage walks in Pune.
sources: J. Fergusson and J. Burgess, The Cave Temples of India (London, 1880), pp. 182, 223–226 and plate IX (plan and section).
Gazetteer of the Bombay Presidency, vol. XVIII, part III, Poona (Bombay, 1885), "Bhaja".
Bharhut stupa relief, early 2nd century BCE, Freer Gallery of Art, Smithsonian, F1932.26 (comparative layer).
J. Marshall, A Guide to Sanchi (3rd edition, 1955) (comparative layer).
Khuddakapāṭha 1 and Majjhima Nikāya 100 (Saṅgārava Sutta), Pali canon (chant layer).
Archaeological Survey of India, list of centrally protected monuments, Mumbai Circle: "Cave temples and inscriptions, Bhaja".

app.heading: Bhaja Caves chaitya hall (Cave 12) in 3D
app.intro: A rock-cut Buddhist prayer hall of about the 2nd century BCE, modelled to the measured survey of 1880. Drag to orbit, pinch to zoom (or click the model, then scroll), switch on the layers along the bottom, or walk the nave in first person.
